title: Design release 1 tells a trader which documents to attach before the upload form; the frontend goes straight to the form with no guidance at all

finding.frontend: Between the "Upload documents" heading and the first field there is nothing. The captured DOM of fe-documents goes from the h1 straight into the form and the Document reference label, and the whole page contains no paragraph of body copy, no bulleted list of document kinds, no details expander and no link out to GOV.UK guidance. A trader arriving on the page is told what to type but never what to attach or why: the words ITAHC, licence, invoice and certificate appear nowhere on the frontend page outside the saved-documents table.
finding.prototype: The page opens with three pieces of guidance before the form. First a paragraph: "You must attach an ITAHC if this consignment requires one. If you do not have it now, you can add it later. All documents should be uploaded before the consignment arrives at the UK port. Documents must be in English and you must upload all pages." Then "Other documents you may need to attach include:" over a bulleted list of "import licences or authorisations" and "commercial documents or invoices". Then a closed details expander, "Check which additional documents you must upload", holding a two-column table headed Consignment / Documents needed with three rows — animals that do not need a health certificate need an exporter's declaration that they are fit to travel; livestock transiting bluetongue restricted territories need Bluetongue declaration GBHC172; rodents imported for research purposes need an RM39 licence and supplementary health certificate — followed by "Check the documents you need on GOV.UK (opens in a new tab)", linked to the GOV.UK import-of-products guidance. All of it is stated at app/views/upload-documents.html:37-79.
finding.difference: Add the guidance block to the frontend's documents template above the form: the intro paragraph, the "Other documents you may need to attach include" list, and a govukDetails expander holding the three-row table and the GOV.UK link. The copy belongs in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/copy/copy.en.js and the markup in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/template.njk:16-17, before the form element opens. This is content only — no new field, no validation, no service call — so it can be built today. The GOV.UK href in Design release 1 carries prototype analytics parameters; use the clean guidance URL. Raised as one finding rather than three because it is one block of page content that only makes sense together. It names no control deliberately: the difference is a block of prose above the form, not a field, and the whole-page shot is the right picture for it.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding any body paragraph, bulleted list or govuk-details element between the h1 and the form in the captured DOM of fe-documents. The only govuk-list on that page is the file-requirements hint inside the upload control, and there is no govuk-details element on the page at all.
finding.verification: Ran the falsifier against capture/html/frontend/fe-documents.html: the h1 is immediately followed by the form element and the crumb input, there is no govuk-details anywhere on the page (grep count 0) and the only govuk-list--bullet is the two-bullet file hint inside the upload control. Read app/views/upload-documents.html:37-81 on the DR1 side and confirmed the intro paragraph, the "Other documents you may need to attach include:" list and the details expander with its three-row Consignment / Documents needed table and the GOV.UK link, all in the root view rather than a release subfolder. Opened both screenshots: the DR1 page shows all three blocks above the File upload panel and the frontend page shows none of them. CORRECT.
finding.correction: CLAIMED, in passing: "the words ITAHC, licence, invoice and certificate appear nowhere on the frontend page outside the saved-documents table". TRUE of ITAHC, invoice and certificate — zero occurrences of each in fe-documents.html. Not quite true of "licence": the word appears four times, all of them in the page footer's Open Government Licence notice and its class names, which is chrome and has nothing to do with document guidance. The slot is left as it stands because the claim it supports — that the page offers no guidance about what to attach — is unaffected.
